entries.title: About SFAF
entries.content: San Francisco AIDS Foundation promotes health, wellness, and social justice for communities most impacted by HIV, through sexual health and substance use services, advocacy, and community partnerships. It envisions a future where health justice is achieved for all people living with or at risk for HIV. Services are provided at Strut (the clinic in the Castro), the main office, and the 6th Street Center. Federal EIN: 94-2927405. The page also links to SFAF's strategic plan, impact report, leadership, and board of directors.

entries.title: Contact Us
entries.content: The quickest way to reach SFAF is email: info@sfaf.org. Mailing address and main phone: 940 Howard Street, San Francisco, CA 94103, 415-487-3000. Press inquiries: media@sfaf.org or 415-487-8064. Questions about donating: development@sfaf.org or 415-487-3092. Social media: @sfaidsfound on Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and YouTube. Hours are on the Locations & Hours page. This is the default fallback when a question can't be answered confidently.

entries.title: Locations & Hours
entries.content: Main Office: 940 Howard Street, San Francisco, CA 94103 (two blocks from Powell Street Station). Phone 415-487-3000. Mon–Fri, 9:30 am to 5 pm. Strut: 470 Castro Street, San Francisco, CA 94114. Phone 415-581-1600. Tue–Sat, 10 am to 7 pm (closed 1 to 3 pm on Fridays). Sexual health services, HIV and STI testing and treatment, PrEP and PEP, substance use treatment and support services. 6th Street Center: 117 6th Street, San Francisco, CA 94103. Comprehensive, free, low-threshold health services, treatment, and supplies for people who use drugs in SoMa. Hours: Mon 11–7, Tue 11–8, Wed 11–7, Thu 11–9, Fri 11–7. Scheduled services there: medical care (wound care, HIV/hep C testing and treatment, basic medical care, PrEP) Mon–Fri 11 am–5 pm; hep C treatment program Wednesdays 11 am–5 pm; onsite buprenorphine from SFDPH Street Medicine Tuesdays 1:30–5 pm; contingency management Mon, Wed, Fri 6–8 pm; substance use counseling by Harm Reduction Therapy Center Tue and Thu 5–8 pm. Community health drop-in sites (treatment connections and supplies that reduce risk of HIV, hepatitis C, and overdose): Martin de Porres House of Hospitality, 225 Potrero Ave (between 15th and 16th), Wednesdays 12–2 pm; Mission Neighborhood Resource Center, 165 Capp Street (between 16th and 17th), Fridays 3–5 pm. No e-bikes, e-scooters, or other battery-powered vehicles are allowed inside SFAF sites.

entries.title: Health Services
entries.content: Overview of SFAF health services, offered across three locations and mobile health access sites: sexual health services, HIV & STI testing, PrEP & PEP, HIV services, trans health care, substance use treatment, services for people who use drugs, overdose prevention & response, hepatitis C testing & treatment, drug checking, and a full-service pharmacy at Strut, 470 Castro St. SFAF welcomes people of any gender identity and sexual orientation, with an emphasis on serving the LGBTQ+ community. Clinic appointments are made through the Sexual Health Clinical Services page.

entries.title: Sexual Health Clinical Services (Clinic Appointments)
entries.content: Sexual health and HIV services at Strut, 470 Castro Street, San Francisco. Make an appointment at 415-581-1600 or book online from this page; a limited number of same-day drop-in appointments are available. If you're not sure what type of appointment to make, call. Services listed: HIV & STI testing, HIV care, PrEP & PEP, STI treatment, Doxy PEP, gender-affirming care, anal health care, condoms and safer sex supplies, and vaccinations (hepatitis A and B, flu shots in fall/winter, mpox JYNNEOS). The clinic has begun billing insurance; most clients pay little or nothing, and care is always provided without regard to ability to pay or insurance status. Medical records requests: medicalrecords@sfaf.org.

entries.title: HIV & STI Testing
entries.content: HIV & STI testing at Strut, 470 Castro Street, San Francisco, for people of any gender identity and sexual orientation. Make an appointment at 415-581-1600 or book online from this page; a limited number of same-day drop-in appointments are available. Appointment types listed: Sexual Health Screening (testing plus a visit with a nurse), Express Sexual Health Screening (testing only, for people with no symptoms), PrEP Enrollment (new clients), and PrEP Follow Up Express (enrolled PrEP clients). If you're not sure which appointment to make, call. The clinic has begun billing insurance (see the billing FAQs).

entries.title: PrEP & PEP
entries.content: PrEP and PEP services at Strut, 470 Castro Street, San Francisco. PEP: if you think you need PEP, call 415-581-1600 to schedule; the page says PEP should be started as soon as possible and within 72 hours of a potential exposure. PrEP: new clients book a PrEP Enrollment visit (can take up to two hours and includes meeting a benefits navigator about ways to pay); follow-up care starts one month later, then every three months. If you've run out of PrEP refills, call 415-581-1600. SFAF does not prescribe PrEP to people covered by Kaiser Permanente, TRICARE, or Veterans Health Administration benefits. An at-home PrEP option is also linked from this page. The clinic has begun billing insurance.

entries.title: HIV Services
entries.content: HIV clinical services at Strut, 470 Castro Street, San Francisco: HIV testing, linkage to long-term HIV care, rapid HIV treatment starts, emergency/interim HIV medications, and benefits navigation including help enrolling in health insurance and benefits. For people living with HIV but out of care, staff can help with lab work, restarting medication, and getting back into medical care. Make an appointment at 415-581-1600; a limited number of same-day drop-in appointments are available. The clinic has begun billing insurance.

entries.title: SFAF Pharmacy
entries.content: Full-service pharmacy at 470 Castro Street, Suite B (first floor of Strut), San Francisco. Hours: Tuesday–Saturday, 10:30 am to 7 pm. Phone 628-777-SFAF (7323); email pharmacy@sfaf.org. Primarily for existing SFAF and Strut clients; outside community members are welcome, though there may be delays for medications not kept in stock. Most clients leave with a same-day fill after their PrEP, HIV, or sexual health visit. Home delivery is available (free for clients). Licensed in California only; cannot ship to other states. Partners with patient assistance and copay card programs to reduce costs for eligible patients.

entries.title: Hepatitis C Testing & Treatment
entries.content: Free hepatitis C testing and treatment at Strut (Castro) and the 6th Street Center (SoMa), including for people who have injected or currently inject drugs. Sobriety or abstinence is not required, and proof of insurance or other documentation is not needed to get started. Visit Strut or the 6th Street Center in person to discuss options. Support includes secure locker storage for medication. See Locations & Hours for times (the 6th Street Center hep C treatment program runs Wednesdays).

entries.title: Trans Health Care
entries.content: Trans-inclusive sexual health and gender-affirming hormone services at Strut, 470 Castro Street, San Francisco. All trans, gender non-binary, genderqueer, and gender non-conforming people are welcome. Services include prescribing and providing gender-affirming hormones, hormone level checks, and hormone injection help or self-injection training, along with sexual health and harm reduction services. Make an appointment at 415-581-1600. The clinic has begun billing insurance.

entries.title: Substance Use Treatment
entries.content: Several paths to substance use treatment and counseling. The Stonewall Project offers outpatient substance use treatment and counseling for gay, bisexual, and queer men, other men who have sex with men, and trans and non-binary people (stonewall@sfaf.org, 415-487-3100). Drop-in substance use counseling at the 6th Street Center (117 6th St.), Tuesdays and Thursdays 5–8 pm. Suboxone through the SFDPH Street Medicine team at the 6th Street Center (visit in person), and linkage to methadone services. A 12-week contingency management program (PROP) for people wanting to reduce, quit, or change their use of meth, cocaine, or other stimulants, at 940 Howard St. (call 415-487-3100) and the 6th Street Center. Referrals to partner programs, including inpatient treatment.

entries.title: Services for People Who Use Drugs
entries.content: Free, low-threshold care for people who use drugs, centered on the 6th Street Center in SoMa: connection to treatment (inpatient, withdrawal, contingency management, outpatient), medications for opioid use disorder including Suboxone and linkage to methadone, naloxone (Narcan), drug checking, safer use supplies including syringes, safe disposal supplies, hepatitis C treatment and medication storage, wound care, first aid, PrEP, and hygiene supplies. To report improperly discarded syringes, call the Pick Up Crew at 415-818-7769, 7 am to 7 pm, 7 days a week, or report to 311.

entries.title: Overdose Prevention & Response
entries.content: Nasal and intramuscular naloxone (Narcan) and overdose recognition and response training, for people who use drugs, people who love them, and people who spend time with others who use drugs, at the 6th Street Center (117 6th Street) during open hours and at mobile sites across San Francisco. Fentanyl test strips are available at the 6th Street Center and mobile sites, and point-of-care drug checking is offered. San Francisco residents who don't use drugs and aren't around people who do are directed to the Community Behavioral Health Services (CBHS) Pharmacy at 1380 Howard Street.

entries.title: Insurance & Billing FAQs
entries.content: The Strut clinic, previously free, now bills insurance. Staff ask for insurance information and a government-issued ID. The vast majority of clients pay $0 or very little out of pocket; preventive services such as HIV/STI testing and PrEP access are generally not subject to a co-pay. Without insurance, visits are charged on a sliding fee scale, and people at or below 300% of the federal poverty level may qualify for free care. Financial assistance and fee waivers are available for eligible clients.

entries.title: Support Services
entries.content: Support services offered at the main office (940 Howard St.), at Strut, and in the community: Aging Services (including the Elizabeth Taylor 50-Plus Network), Black Health (Black Brothers Esteem, TransLife, HUES, case management), Programa Latino, Trans Support, Mental & Behavioral Health, substance use counseling through The Stonewall Project, and Housing Subsidies & Financial Benefits (temporary rental assistance for people living with HIV, and benefits counseling for Medicare, Medi-Cal, HealthySF, and ADAP).

entries.title: The Stonewall Project
entries.content: Harm reduction substance use counseling for queer, gay, bisexual, and same-gender-loving men, and trans and nonbinary people, who are concerned about their drug or alcohol use and considering change. Goals can include complete abstinence, targeted abstinence, or safer use, and there is no requirement to stop or change use. Offers drop-in groups (no intake, no waits), a 12-week contingency management program, an enrolled counseling program (minimum two groups per week), and Enhanced Care Management through San Francisco Health Plan. Virtual and in-person sessions. Contact stonewall@sfaf.org or 415-487-3100. The services schedule is linked from the page.

entries.title: Aging Services
entries.content: Programs focused on health, well-being, and reducing isolation as people age. The Elizabeth Taylor 50-Plus Network serves gay, bisexual, and trans men aged 50 and older, both HIV-negative and living with HIV; become a member by attending an event and giving your contact info. TGI Aging Services include social outings, support groups, and monthly events for trans, gender non-conforming, intersex, and nonbinary community members. Services and activities are usually free, though occasional events may cost money. RSVP to 50Plus@action.sfaf.org or 415-487-3132; general email 50Plusnetwork@sfaf.org.

entries.title: Black Health
entries.content: Programs prioritizing the needs, challenges, joys, and celebrations of Black communities, led by BIPOC staff. Black Brothers Esteem (BBE), established in 1996, for Black same-gender-loving men from their 20s to 80s. TransLife, an inclusive multiracial support group for transgender, non-binary, genderqueer, gender-fluid, and gender non-conforming people. HUES, for Black women across the spectrum of age with reasons for HIV prevention and care. HIV & Aging case management: email blackhealth@sfaf.org.

entries.title: Programa Latino (Latine Health)
entries.content: Outreach and support for Latine community members, especially immigrants and Spanish-only speakers, regardless of immigration status, to help navigate mental health, substance use, harm reduction, and HIV care and prevention. Drop-in hours for new participants: Monday through Friday, 2:30–4:30 pm. Weekly health education group sessions run in two cycles (March–June and September–December); the El Grupo support group meets every Thursday; leadership trainings are delivered in Spanish. Email programalatino@sfaf.org.

entries.title: Mental & Behavioral Health
entries.content: Mental and behavioral health care from licensed practitioners, including care related to substance use, trauma, race, and culture. Individual one-on-one therapy is available in limited amounts. The Stonewall Project offers one-on-one mental health care for gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men and transgender people (stonewall@sfaf.org, 415-487-3100). Twice-monthly support groups are listed for trans Latinas over 50 (in Spanish) and for Black and BIPOC trans community members; contacts for each are on the page.

entries.title: Trans Support
entries.content: Social support, mental health, and community care groups for people who are transgender, non-binary, genderqueer, intersex, and gender expansive. Groups listed: Trans Galaxy Mental Health (twice-monthly drop-in peer support, adults 18+), Transformaciones (twice-monthly drop-in mental health support group for transgender Latine immigrant adults, in Spanish), Beyond the Binary (monthly event series for gender-expansive, intersex, and nonbinary adults 50+), TransLife Drop-In (twice-monthly community space, adults 18+), Glitter 'N Go (monthly outings for active TransLife participants), and the TGI Intergenerational Brunch (monthly, with Openhouse). Contacts for each group are on the page. For trans health care, see Trans Health Care.

entries.title: Housing Subsidies & Financial Benefits
entries.content: Benefits counseling and a rental subsidy program for people living with HIV. The rental subsidy helps people living with HIV and AIDS who are also experiencing poverty secure and maintain housing; referrals come through the MOHCD Plus Housing waitlist, and the program accepts referrals from service providers only, not directly from clients (provider line: SFAF Housing Coalition Line, 415-487-3037). Financial benefits counseling for people living with HIV and AIDS covers programs like Medicare, Medi-Cal, HealthySF, and ADAP: call 415-487-8023.

entries.title: Donate
entries.content: SFAF's secure online donation form. SFAF is a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization, and donations are tax-deductible within the guidelines of U.S. law. Questions about donating: development@sfaf.org or 415-487-3092. For other ways to give (mail, phone, stock, planned giving, memorial gifts), see Ways to Give.

entries.title: Ways to Give
entries.content: Ways to support SFAF: give online through the secure donation form; monthly giving through the Justice Collective; the Foundation Giving Circle for those who give $2,500 or more annually; fundraising events (Cycle to Zero, Santa Skivvies Run, Tribute Gala); brand partnerships and event sponsorship; planned giving (including SFAF in a will or trust); donating stock, securities, or life income; memorial and honor gifts; matching gifts and volunteer grants; some in-kind donations (personal art pieces are not accepted); and car donations through Car Donation Services, Inc. By mail: San Francisco AIDS Foundation, Attn: Donor Services, PO Box 426199, San Francisco, CA 94142-6199. By phone with a credit card: 415-487-3092. Federal EIN: 94-2927405.

entries.title: Get Involved
entries.content: Ways to get involved with SFAF: giving, planned giving, partnerships, volunteering, the SFAF Ambassador Council, advocacy, and events held throughout the year (Cycle to Zero, Tribute Gala, Santa Skivvies Run). There is also an SFAF Shop.

entries.title: Volunteer
entries.content: Volunteers help at fundraising events (Cycle to Zero, Tribute Gala, Santa Skivvies Run) and help connect clients with care services. Teams can sponsor a kit-packing event through Pack with a Purpose. Current opportunities are listed in the Volunteer Portal at volunteers.sfaf.org, linked from this page. The SFAF Ambassador Council is another way to support the organization.

entries.title: Events
entries.content: SFAF's signature fundraising events: Cycle to Zero, a three-day cycling journey through San Francisco and the Russian River region; Tribute Gala, SFAF's premier fundraising event; and Santa Skivvies Run, its most festive fundraising event. There is also a DIY fundraising option and corporate sponsorship opportunities. Dates and registration are on this page.

entries.title: Sign Up for SFAF News
entries.content: Sign up to get the latest news and top articles from SFAF delivered to your inbox.

entries.title: Servicios en español
entries.content: Spanish-language overview of SFAF services. Services are offered to anyone regardless of immigration status ('Ofrecemos servicios a cualquier persona sin importar su situación migratoria'). Listed services include access to HIV care, the Grupo de Apoyo Latino and a support group for Latina women living with HIV, housing subsidies for people living with HIV, hepatitis C treatment, PrEP, PEP, Doxy PEP, sexual health care including HIV and STI testing, gender-affirming hormones, harm reduction and overdose prevention, and safer drug and alcohol use. Spanish-language line: 415-632-9722. Locations: Strut, 470 Castro Street (between Market and 18th), 415-581-1600; 6th Street Center, 117 6th Street (between Mission and Minna); main office, 940 Howard Street, 415-487-3000.
